name: Isotropic Gaussian Scale Contraction
definition: A technique to contract the scale of isotropic Gaussians under a scene contraction function C(x) by linearizing the contraction around each Gaussian center x_j to produce the Jacobian J_C(x_j), then deriving an isotropic scale from the determinant of this Jacobian. This avoids the expensive general multivariate Gaussian contraction used in mip-NeRF 360.
summary: Isotropic Gaussian Scale Contraction efficiently adapts Gaussian scales in contracted spaces using a Jacobian determinant, avoiding the computational overhead of full covariance matrix transformations.
